capabilities: Open multiple terminal tabs inside Obsidian and split, pin or drag them like note tabs
Launch shells and CLI tools through automatically detected or custom shell profiles
Cmd/Ctrl+click vault file paths and web links in terminal output to open them
Send selected note text or the current line to the shell
Search, copy, rename, duplicate and restore terminal tabs across restarts
extras: The README states the plugin has no network access, telemetry or accounts, and documents known limitations (untested popout windows, clickable paths only for vault files without spaces, no current-folder tracking on Windows without OSC 7).
motivation: The README explains that Obsidian's native node-pty module would need recompiling for every release, so the author built a Python-based PTY bridge instead.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in terminal, so running shell commands or CLI tools next to your notes requires switching to a separate application.

relations.evidence: Run your shell — or a tool such as Claude Code — right next to your notes.

summary: Integrated terminal that opens real PTY shell tabs inside Obsidian, started in the vault folder.
